raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## What does this PR do?

Removes hardware-dependent dispatch from `verl.utils.attention_utils` and makes the existing pure PyTorch/einops padding helpers the shared implementation on every PyTorch device. The redundant `npu_flash_attn_utils.py` copy is removed.

The public index helpers also normalize indices to `torch.int64`, so direct callers can safely pass either `int32` or `int64` indices to gather/scatter/indexing operations.

## Why this approach?

The NPU implementation was already copied from flash-attn and only uses PyTorch and einops, so selecting it based on available hardware was unnecessary.

I did not directly replace it with Transformers' private `_index_first_axis`. That helper merges the first two input dimensions, whereas verl and flash-attn expect the input to already be flattened along the first dimension. Direct replacement would silently turn an `(N, 1)` result into `(N,)`.

The shared implementation retains the existing verl/flash-attn shape, metadata, and gradient semantics.

## Duplicate-work check

Before implementation and again before the latest update, I checked issue #7088 and searched open PRs by the issue number and by `attention_utils`, `index_first_axis`, `pad_input`, and `npu_flash_attn_utils`. No overlapping implementation was found. Draft PR #7172 explicitly depends on this PR and is downstream work.

Closes #7088.

## Tests

Validated commit: `0835ff4437b2e886417b0c4c5ed2fbe8444437bd`, rebased onto main `393b03a089a812971aeff303eaeb466456693d8a`.

- CPU, Python 3.12.13, PyTorch 2.9.1+cpu:
  - `python -m pytest -q tests/utils/test_attention_utils_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_attention_utils.py`
  - `2 passed, 9 skipped` (accelerator-only cases skipped as intended).
- CUDA, PyTorch 2.6.0+cu124, 8 x RTX 3090:
  - `for i in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$i python -m pytest -q tests/utils/test_attention_utils.py; done`
  - 9 tests passed on each GPU, 72 total. Coverage includes FP32/FP16/BF16 values, int32/int64 indices, bool masks, forward/backward, and pad/unpad round trips.
- Latest-main repository checks:
  - `python -m pre_commit run --files verl/utils/attention_utils.py tests/utils/test_attention_utils_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_attention_utils.py`
  - All 13 hooks passed, including ruff, format, mypy, test structure, naming, license, device API, and compileall.
- Exact old/new baseline comparison on CPU and CUDA:
  - outputs, indices, sequence metadata, round-trip tensors, and gradients matched with `rtol=0, atol=0`.
- Static reference audit:
  - no Python references to the removed `verl.utils.npu_flash_attn_utils` remain.

### NPU validation limitation

No Ascend device is available locally. The new `tests/utils/test_attention_utils.py` is intentionally named so the existing `NPU unit tests` workflow collects it directly. `model_ascend` also exercises the downstream transformer, FSDP rmpad, and Ulysses call paths, while `e2e_ascend` supplies full training coverage. These fork workflows are currently awaiting maintainer approval; this PR does not claim NPU runtime success until those jobs run.

## Code Review

This pull request refactors `verl/utils/attention_utils.py` to replace the dynamic device-specific dispatching with a unified, device-agnostic implementation using PyTorch and einops. It also adds CPU-based unit tests for these attention utility functions. The code review identified critical compatibility issues in the new implementation: `torch.gather` and `torch.scatter_` require `int64` indices and will fail if `int32` tensors are passed, and using the `+` operator on boolean masks will raise a runtime error in PyTorch and should be replaced with the bitwise OR `|` operator.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The [consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-repo-code) is being sunset. Starting **June 18, 2026**, new organization installations will be blocked, and all code review activity will officially cease on **July 17, 2026**.
> For more details on the timeline and next steps, please review the [Help Documentation](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review).

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

In PyTorch, `torch.gather` strictly requires the `index` tensor to be of type `torch.int64` (`LongTensor`). If `indices` is passed as `torch.int32` (which is very common in optimized attention/padding pipelines to save memory), this will result in a runtime `RuntimeError: gather(): Expected dtype int64 for index`.

To prevent this, cast `indices` to `.long()` before repeating and gathering.

```suggestion
        return torch.gather(
            rearrange(input, "b ... -> b (...)"),
            0,
            repeat(indices.long(), "z -> z d", d=second_dim),
        ).reshape(-1, *other_shape)
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Similarly to the forward pass, `torch.scatter_` strictly requires the `index` tensor to be of type `torch.int64` (`LongTensor`). If `indices` is `torch.int32`, this will raise a runtime `RuntimeError: scatter(): Expected dtype int64 for index`.

Cast `indices` to `.long()` to ensure compatibility with `int32` index tensors.

```suggestion
        grad_input.scatter_(0, repeat(indices.long(), "z -> z d", d=grad_output.shape[1]), grad_output)
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Using the `+` operator on boolean tensors is not supported in PyTorch and will raise a `RuntimeError: Addition, the '+' operator, with two bool tensors is not supported. Use the '|' operator or torch.logical_or() instead.`.

Since `attention_mask` and `unused_mask` are commonly boolean tensors in LLM pipelines, you should use the bitwise OR operator `|` (or `torch.logical_or`) instead of `+`. This is fully compatible with both boolean and integer tensors.

```suggestion
    all_masks = (attention_mask | unused_mask) if unused_mask is not None else attention_mask
```

+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from verl.utils.attention_utils import index_first_axis, pad_input, unpad_input
+from verl.utils.device import get_device_name, get_torch_device
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not get_torch_device().is_available(), reason="requires an accelerator")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("indices_dtype", [torch.int32, torch.int64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("values_dtype", [torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+def test_index_first_axis_on_accelerator(indices_dtype, values_dtype):
+    device = get_device_name()
+    hidden_states = torch.arange(48, dtype=torch.float32, device=device).to(values_dtype)
+    hidden_states = hidden_states.reshape(8, 2, 3).requires_grad_()
+    indices = torch.tensor([0, 3, 7], dtype=indices_dtype, device=device)
+
+    selected = index_first_axis(hidden_states, indices)
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(selected, hidden_states.detach()[indices.long()])
+    selected.sum().backward()
+    expected_grad = torch.zeros_like(hidden_states)
+    expected_grad[indices.long()] = 1
+    torch.testing.assert_close(hidden_states.grad, expected_grad)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("values_dtype", [torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+def test_pad_and_unpad_bool_masks_on_accelerator(values_dtype):
+    device = get_device_name()
+    hidden_states = torch.arange(24, dtype=torch.float32, device=device).to(values_dtype)
+    hidden_states = hidden_states.reshape(2, 4, 3).requires_grad_()
+    attention_mask = torch.tensor([[1, 1, 0, 0], [1, 0, 1, 0]], dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
+    unused_mask = torch.tensor([[0, 0, 1, 0], [0, 1, 0, 0]], dtype=torch.bool, device=device)
+
+    unpadded, indices, cu_seqlens, max_seqlen, used_seqlens = unpad_input(
+        hidden_states,
+        attention_mask,
+        unused_mask,
+    )
+    padded = pad_input(unpadded, indices.to(torch.int32), batch=2, seqlen=4)
+
+    selected_mask = (attention_mask | unused_mask).unsqueeze(-1)
+    expected = torch.where(selected_mask, hidden_states.detach(), torch.zeros_like(hidden_states))
+    torch.testing.assert_close(padded, expected)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(indices, torch.tensor([0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 6], device=device))
+    torch.testing.assert_close(cu_seqlens, torch.tensor([0, 3, 6], dtype=torch.int32, device=device))
+    torch.testing.assert_close(used_seqlens, torch.tensor([2, 2], dtype=torch.int32, device=device))
+    assert max_seqlen == 3
+
+    padded.sum().backward()
+    expected_grad = selected_mask.expand_as(hidden_states).to(hidden_states.dtype)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(hidden_states.grad, expected_grad)

+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+from einops import rearrange, repeat
+
+
+# Adapted from https://github.com/Dao-AILab/flash-attention/blob/main/flash_attn/bert_padding.py.
+# These operations use only PyTorch and einops, so the same implementation works on every PyTorch device.
+class IndexFirstAxis(torch.autograd.Function):
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, input, indices):
+        assert indices.ndim == 1
+        indices = indices.long()
+        ctx.save_for_backward(indices)
+        assert input.ndim >= 2
+        ctx.first_axis_dim, other_shape = input.shape[0], input.shape[1:]
+        second_dim = other_shape.numel()
+        return torch.gather(
+            rearrange(input, "b ... -> b (...)"),
+            0,
+            repeat(indices, "z -> z d", d=second_dim),
+        ).reshape(-1, *other_shape)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def backward(ctx, grad_output):
+        (indices,) = ctx.saved_tensors
+        assert grad_output.ndim >= 2
+        other_shape = grad_output.shape[1:]
+        grad_output = rearrange(grad_output, "b ... -> b (...)")
+        grad_input = torch.zeros(
+            [ctx.first_axis_dim, grad_output.shape[1]],
+            device=grad_output.device,
+            dtype=grad_output.dtype,
+        )
+        grad_input.scatter_(0, repeat(indices, "z -> z d", d=grad_output.shape[1]), grad_output)
+        return grad_input.reshape(ctx.first_axis_dim, *other_shape), None
+
+
+index_first_axis = IndexFirstAxis.apply
+
+
+class IndexPutFirstAxis(torch.autograd.Function):
+    @staticmethod
+    def forward(ctx, values, indices, first_axis_dim):
+        assert indices.ndim == 1
+        indices = indices.long()
+        ctx.save_for_backward(indices)
+        assert values.ndim >= 2
+        output = torch.zeros(first_axis_dim, *values.shape[1:], device=values.device, dtype=values.dtype)
+        output[indices] = values
+        return output
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def backward(ctx, grad_output):
+        (indices,) = ctx.saved_tensors
+        return grad_output[indices], None, None
+
+
+index_put_first_axis = IndexPutFirstAxis.apply
+
+
+def pad_input(hidden_states, indices, batch, seqlen):
+    """Restore unpadded hidden states to shape ``(batch, seqlen, ...)``."""
+    output = index_put_first_axis(hidden_states, indices, batch * seqlen)
+    return rearrange(output, "(b s) ... -> b s ...", b=batch)
+
+
+def unpad_input(hidden_states, attention_mask, unused_mask=None):
+    """Remove padding and return FlashAttention-compatible sequence metadata."""
+    all_masks = (attention_mask + unused_mask) if unused_mask is not None else attention_mask
+    seqlens_in_batch = all_masks.sum(dim=-1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    used_seqlens_in_batch = attention_mask.sum(dim=-1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    indices = torch.nonzero(all_masks.flatten(), as_tuple=False).flatten()
+    max_seqlen_in_batch = seqlens_in_batch.max().item()
+    cu_seqlens = F.pad(torch.cumsum(seqlens_in_batch, dim=0, dtype=torch.int32), (1, 0))
+    return (
+        index_first_axis(rearrange(hidden_states, "b s ... -> (b s) ..."), indices),
+        indices,
+        cu_seqlens,
+        max_seqlen_in_batch,
+        used_seqlens_in_batch,
+    )
 
 
 __all__ = ["index_first_axis", "pad_input", "rearrange", "unpad_input"]

-        output = torch.zeros(first_axis_dim, *values.shape[1:], device=values.device, dtype=values.dtype)
-        # TD [2022-03-04] For some reason torch.scatter is a bit faster than indexing.

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

In PyTorch, `torch.gather` strictly requires the `index` tensor to be of type `torch.int64` (`LongTensor`). If `indices` is passed as `torch.int32` (which is very common in optimized attention/padding pipelines to save memory), this will result in a runtime `RuntimeError: gather(): Expected dtype int64 for index`.

To prevent this, cast `indices` to `.long()` before repeating and gathering.

```suggestion
        return torch.gather(
            rearrange(input, "b ... -> b (...)"),
            0,
            repeat(indices.long(), "z -> z d", d=second_dim),
        ).reshape(-1, *other_shape)
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Similarly to the forward pass, `torch.scatter_` strictly requires the `index` tensor to be of type `torch.int64` (`LongTensor`). If `indices` is `torch.int32`, this will raise a runtime `RuntimeError: scatter(): Expected dtype int64 for index`.

Cast `indices` to `.long()` to ensure compatibility with `int32` index tensors.

```suggestion
        grad_input.scatter_(0, repeat(indices.long(), "z -> z d", d=grad_output.shape[1]), grad_output)
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Using the `+` operator on boolean tensors is not supported in PyTorch and will raise a `RuntimeError: Addition, the '+' operator, with two bool tensors is not supported. Use the '|' operator or torch.logical_or() instead.`.

Since `attention_mask` and `unused_mask` are commonly boolean tensors in LLM pipelines, you should use the bitwise OR operator `|` (or `torch.logical_or`) instead of `+`. This is fully compatible with both boolean and integer tensors.

```suggestion
    all_masks = (attention_mask | unused_mask) if unused_mask is not None else attention_mask
```

## Code Review

This pull request refactors `verl/utils/attention_utils.py` to replace the dynamic device-specific dispatching with a unified, device-agnostic implementation using PyTorch and einops. It also adds CPU-based unit tests for these attention utility functions. The code review identified critical compatibility issues in the new implementation: `torch.gather` and `torch.scatter_` require `int64` indices and will fail if `int32` tensors are passed, and using the `+` operator on boolean masks will raise a runtime error in PyTorch and should be replaced with the bitwise OR `|` operator.
